title: Driving Distance Calculator: Road Miles and Time
description: Calculate driving distance and duration along real roads with the Driving Distance Calculator — open routing data, miles and km. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, two cities 190 miles apart as the crow flies routinely measure 215 or more by road — this calculator is the one that reports the road's answer.
quick_answer: The Driving Distance Calculator measures the distance and duration of a journey along roads, using open routing data. Set an origin and a destination and read the road distance in miles and kilometres with the driving time — the figure fuel, cost and day plans should all be built from.

A round's total road distance is its cost skeleton — drivers, fuel and time all hang off this number.

New York to Boston is approx. 190.2 miles straight-line. The road journey is materially longer — interstates are direct by road standards, not by geometry's. Every plan built on 190 meets reality at the first fuel stop.

Mountain and coastal pairs show the biggest gaps between straight-line and road figures. The ratio between the two — visible by comparing this page with Distance Between Two Places — is a fingerprint of the terrain.

faq: No. The duration is the routing engine's estimate for the road network, without current traffic. Add your own margin for the hour you will actually travel.
Why is road distance longer than straight-line distance?
Roads follow terrain, property and history; the straight line follows geometry. Bridges, passes and junctions all add their share.
Can route results change over time?
Slightly, as the open road data improves and roads themselves change. The pair you measured last year deserves a fresh run before this year's trip.
Which routing data does it use?
Open routing over OpenStreetMap data — the same open network this site's other routing tools use, so results are consistent across them.
Shortest or fastest — which route is measured?
The router returns its route for the pair; where alternatives matter, compare the figures with the journey's purpose: miles for cost, time for arrival.
Can I use the distance for a mileage claim?
Yes — it is the driven distance, which is what claims reimburse. Keep the pair and date with the claim.
Why does my car show a different distance?
Odometers, route choices and data snapshots differ at the margins. A percent or two is normal; a tenth is a different route.
Does it measure for trucks or cars?
The network routing is car-oriented open data. Truck restrictions (weight, height, hazmat) are a specialist layer this page does not apply.
Can I measure a round trip?
Route out and back: one-way distance × 2 unless the return differs — measure the return pair separately if the roads force a different way back.
